items.title: Absolutely continuous curves of order two in Wasserstein space

references.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures, Theorem 1.1.2 and Chapter 8, PDF pp. 24–26 and 171–186
Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §§5.1–5.3, PDF pp. 161–178

items.statement: Fix $T>0$. A curve $\mu:[0,T]\to\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$ is absolutely continuous of order two, written $\mu\in AC^2([0,T];\mathcal P_2)$, if it is continuous in $W_2$ and there is a nonnegative Lebesgue-measurable $g$ with $\int_0^T g(t)^2dt<\infty$ such that $W_2(\mu_s,\mu_t)\le\int_s^t g(r)dr$ for every $0\le s\le t\le T$. At an interior time $t$ where the limit exists, the metric derivative is $|\dot\mu_t|=\lim_{h\to0}W_2(\mu_{t+h},\mu_t)/|h|$; no endpoint derivative is required.

items.title: A narrow probability curve defines its space-time measure

references.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures, Theorem 1.1.2 and Chapter 8, PDF pp. 24–26 and 171–186
Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §§5.1–5.3, PDF pp. 161–178

items.statement: Let $T>0$ and let $t\mapsto\mu_t$ be a narrowly continuous curve of Borel probability measures on $\mathbb R^d$, where narrow continuity means convergence against every bounded continuous real test function. For a product-Borel set $E\subseteq[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d$, write $E_t=\{x:(t,x)\in E\}$ and define $M(E)=\int_0^T\mu_t(E_t)dt$. Then $t\mapsto\mu_t$ is a probability kernel, $M$ is a finite Borel measure of total mass $T$, and for every nonnegative product-Borel $f$, $\int f\,dM=\int_0^T\int f(t,x)d\mu_t(x)dt$.

items.title: Finite-action continuity equation in Euclidean space

references.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures, Theorem 1.1.2 and Chapter 8, PDF pp. 24–26 and 171–186
Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §§5.1–5.3, PDF pp. 161–178

items.statement:
Fix $T>0$ and an integer $d\ge1$. Let $t\mapsto\mu_t$ be a narrowly continuous curve in $\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$ (so $t\mapsto\int f\,d\mu_t$ is continuous for every bounded continuous $f$), let $M$ be its space-time measure $M(dt,dx)=dt\,\mu_t(dx)$, and let $v:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ be Borel. Its squared action is $A(\mu,v)=\int|v(t,x)|^2dM(t,x)$. If $A(\mu,v)<\infty$, say that $v$ solves the continuity equation for $\mu$ when
$$\int_0^T\!\int_{\mathbb R^d}(\partial_t\varphi(t,x)+\nabla_x\varphi(t,x)\cdot v(t,x))\,d\mu_t(x)\,dt=0$$
for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty((0,T)\times\mathbb R^d)$. This is the distributional meaning of $\partial_t\mu_t+\nabla\cdot(v_t\mu_t)=0$; the continuous representative fixes the endpoint laws.

items.title: Gluing two Euclidean couplings
items.axiom_use: Full AC is used for the two standard-Borel disintegrations; this finite gluing uses no further selection.

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $d_1,d_2,d_3\ge1$, let $\alpha$ be a Borel probability on $\mathbb R^{d_1}\times\mathbb R^{d_2}$ and $\beta$ a Borel probability on $\mathbb R^{d_2}\times\mathbb R^{d_3}$, and suppose the second marginal of $\alpha$ and first marginal of $\beta$ are the same probability $\rho$ on $\mathbb R^{d_2}$. There is a Borel probability $\gamma$ on $\mathbb R^{d_1}\times\mathbb R^{d_2}\times\mathbb R^{d_3}$ whose $(x,y)$ marginal is $\alpha$ and whose $(y,z)$ marginal is $\beta$.

items.title: Optimal quadratic couplings exist and their cost is weakly lower semicontinuous
items.axiom_use: AC supplies a sequence of approximate minimizers and the Prokhorov subsequence extractions; Prokhorov's Countable Choice use is inherited from AC.

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every pair $\mu,
u\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$, the infimum of $\int|x-y|^2d\pi(x,y)$ over couplings $\pi$ of $\mu$ and $
u$ is finite and is attained. If $\mu_n,
u_n\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$, $\mu_n$ converges narrowly to $\mu$, and $
u_n$ converges narrowly to $
u$, then
$$W_2(\mu,
u)^2\le\liminf_{n	o\infty}W_2(\mu_n,
u_n)^2.$$

items.title: The quadratic Wasserstein distance is a metric
items.axiom_use: AC is used by the optimal-coupling and gluing suppliers; this theorem adds no choice principle beyond those supplied arguments.

references.title: Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §§5.1–5.3, PDF pp. 161–178
Lénaïc Chizat and Francis Bach, On the Global Convergence of Gradient Descent for Over-parameterized Models using Optimal Transport, Appendix A.1, PDF pp. 12–13

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every integer $d\ge1$, the function $W_2$ defined on $\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$ is a metric: for all $\mu,
u,\lambda\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$ it is finite and nonnegative, $W_2(\mu,
u)=0$ exactly when $\mu=
u$, $W_2(\mu,
u)=W_2(
u,\mu)$, and $W_2(\mu,\lambda)\le W_2(\mu,
u)+W_2(
u,\lambda)$.

items.title: The quadratic Wasserstein space is complete
items.axiom_use: Full AC is used to choose a rapidly Cauchy subsequence, optimal pair couplings, and a Prokhorov subsequence; it supplies the countable/dependent choice used for countable-product compactness.

references.title: Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §§5.1–5.3, PDF pp. 161–178
Lénaïc Chizat and Francis Bach, On the Global Convergence of Gradient Descent for Over-parameterized Models using Optimal Transport, Appendix A.1, PDF pp. 12–13

items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. The metric space $(\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d),W_2)$ is complete: every $W_2$-Cauchy sequence converges in $W_2$ to an element of $\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$.

items.title: The topology of W2 is narrow convergence plus uniform second-moment tails
items.axiom_use: AC enters through existence of optimal couplings. The finite partition, matching, and residual product coupling argument makes no further selections beyond finite choices.

references.title: Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §§5.1–5.3, PDF pp. 161–178
Lénaïc Chizat and Francis Bach, On the Global Convergence of Gradient Descent for Over-parameterized Models using Optimal Transport, Appendix A.1, PDF pp. 12–13

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For $d\ge1$ and $\mu_n,\mu\in\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d)$, $W_2(\mu_n,\mu)\to0$ if and only if $\mu_n$ converges narrowly to $\mu$ and
$$\lim_{R\to\infty}\sup_{n\ge1}\int_{\{|x|>R\}}|x|^2d\mu_n(x)=0.$$
Tightness by itself is insufficient: for $e_1=(1,0,\ldots,0)$ and $\mu_n=(1-n^{-2})\delta_0+n^{-2}\delta_{ne_1}$, the sequence is tight and converges narrowly to $\delta_0$, but $W_2(\mu_n,\delta_0)=1$ for every $n$.

items.title: Metric derivatives of AC2 Wasserstein curves
items.axiom_use: The scalar absolutely-continuous FTC requires Countable and Dependent Choice; AC supplies both. The distance family is explicitly indexed by rational times.

references.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures, Theorem 1.1.2, PDF pp. 24–26
Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §5.2, PDF pp. 168–172

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. If $T>0$ and $\mu\in AC^2([0,T];\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d))$, then the metric derivative
$$|\dot\mu_t|=\lim_{h\to0}\frac{W_2(\mu_{t+h},\mu_t)}{|h|}$$
exists for almost every $t\in(0,T)$, is measurable and belongs to $L^2(0,T)$. For all $0\le s\le t\le T$,
$$W_2(\mu_s,\mu_t)\le\int_s^t|\dot\mu_r|dr.$$
It is the least nonnegative square-integrable upper control: if $g\in L^2(0,T)$ and $W_2(\mu_s,\mu_t)\le\int_s^t g(r)dr$ for all $s\le t$, then $|\dot\mu_t|\le g(t)$ almost everywhere.

items.title: Gaussian regularization preserves finite-action continuity equations

references.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures, Chapter 8, §§8.1–8.2, PDF pp. 171–182
Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §5.3, PDF pp. 173–178

items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $T>0$, $d\ge1$, and let $(\mu_t,v_t)$ be a narrowly continuous finite-action solution of the continuity equation on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d$, with space-time law $M(dt,dx)=dt\,\mu_t(dx)$. For $\varepsilon>0$, let $\rho_\varepsilon$ be the strictly positive centered Gaussian probability density with covariance $\varepsilon I_d$, and define
$$p_t^\varepsilon(x)=\int\rho_\varepsilon(x-y)d\mu_t(y),\quad j_t^\varepsilon(x)=\int\rho_\varepsilon(x-y)v_t(y)d\mu_t(y),\quad v_t^\varepsilon(x)=j_t^\varepsilon(x)/p_t^\varepsilon(x).$$
Then $p_t^\varepsilon$ is a strictly positive smooth probability density for each $t$, $t\mapsto\mu_t^\varepsilon$ is narrowly continuous, $v_t^\varepsilon$ is Borel and locally Lipschitz in $x$ with local magnitude and Lipschitz bounds integrable in time, and $(\mu_t*\rho_\varepsilon,v_t^\varepsilon)$ solves the continuity equation. For almost every $t$,
$$\int|v_t^\varepsilon(x)|^2p_t^\varepsilon(x)dx\le\int|v_t(y)|^2d\mu_t(y).$$

items.title: Quadratic path energy is lower semicontinuous
items.axiom_use: AC supplies Countable and Dependent Choice for the Radon C_c-density, Hilbert Riesz, and scalar Lebesgue FTC suppliers.

references.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures, Chapter 8, §8.2, PDF pp. 179–182
Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §5.3, PDF pp. 176–178

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $T>0$ and give $C([0,T];\mathbb R^d)$ the uniform topology. Define
$$\mathcal E(\gamma)=\begin{cases}\int_0^T|\dot\gamma(t)|^2dt,&\gamma\text{ is absolutely continuous with }\dot\gamma\in L^2(0,T;\mathbb R^d),\\+\infty,&\text{otherwise.}\end{cases}$$
Then $\mathcal E$ is lower semicontinuous. More precisely,
$$\mathcal E(\gamma)=\sup_{0=t_0<\cdots<t_N=T}\sum_{i=0}^{N-1}\frac{|\gamma(t_{i+1})-\gamma(t_i)|^2}{t_{i+1}-t_i},$$
where the supremum is over all finite partitions of $[0,T]$.

items.title: Euclidean spaces admit a smooth compactly supported unit-mass bump
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice enters through the box-measure and product-Lebesgue suppliers; the explicit one-dimensional construction is choice-free.

references.title: MIT 18.102, Chapter 4, §9 Convolution, Lemma 58, printed pp. 136–137

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For every integer $d\ge1$ there is a nonnegative function $\rho_d:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ with continuous partial derivatives of every order, support exactly $[-1,1]^d$, strictly positive on $(-1,1)^d$, and Lebesgue integral $\int_{\mathbb R^d}\rho_d(x)\,dx=1$. Here the support is the closure of the set where the function is nonzero.

items.title: Smooth compactly supported tests are dense for finite Radon L2 measures
items.axiom_use: Dependent Choice is used for C_c density and implies Countable Choice for the local bump and mollifier smoothness; AC supplies both branches in downstream arguments.

references.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures, Chapter 8, §8.2, PDF pp. 179–182
Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §5.3, PDF pp. 176–178

items.statement: Assume Dependent Choice. Let $M$ be a finite Radon Borel measure on $\mathbb R^n$, where $n\ge1$. Then $C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n)$ is dense in $L^2(M)$.

items.title: Local flows for time-measurable fields with integrable local bounds
items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is used only through the scalar Lebesgue FTC to identify derivatives of time integrals; the contraction and flow construction make no further choice.

references.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures, Chapter 8, §§8.1–8.2, PDF pp. 171–182

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. Let $T>0$, let $d\ge1$, and let $b:[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ be Borel. Suppose that for every compact $K\subset\mathbb R^d$ there are nonnegative $m_K,L_K\in L^1(0,T)$ such that for almost every $t$, $|b(t,x)|\le m_K(t)$ and $|b(t,x)-b(t,y)|\le L_K(t)|x-y|$ for all $x,y\in K$. For each $(s,x_0)$ there is a unique maximal absolutely continuous solution $X(\cdot;s,x_0)$ of $\dot X=b(t,X)$ with $X(s)=x_0$, where maximal means that it has no solution extension to a strictly larger interval in $[0,T]$; any maximal endpoint lying in $(0,T)$ can occur only if the trajectory leaves every compact subset of $\mathbb R^d$. If, in addition, $b(t,\cdot)$ is continuously differentiable for almost every $t$ and $D_xb$ has integrable local bounds, then the set of initial points whose trajectories exist between any fixed pair of times is open, its time map is one-to-one onto an open image with both map and inverse continuously differentiable, and the path map into the uniform path space is continuous on the set of trajectories existing through the full interval. On compact flow tubes the dependence on the starting time is locally absolutely continuous and satisfies $\partial_sX(t;s,x)=-D_xX(t;s,x)b(s,x)$ for almost every s, simultaneously for x in the tube. The spatial derivative $V_t=D_{x_0}X(t;s,x_0)$ satisfies $\dot V_t=D_xb(t,X_t)V_t$, $V_s=I_d$, almost everywhere.

items.title: Regularized continuity equations are represented by characteristic flows
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited through Gaussian normalization and inner regularity and supplies Countable Choice for the normalized bump, mollifier, and local flow interfaces. Finite action excludes explosion in both time directions without further selection.

references.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures, Propositions 8.1.7–8.1.10, PDF pp. 173–178
Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §5.3, PDF pp. 173–178

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $(\mu_t^\varepsilon,v_t^\varepsilon)$ be the Gaussian-regularized solution from the preceding lemma on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d$, and write $\mu_t^\varepsilon=p_t^\varepsilon(x)dx$. There is a unique maximal local flow $X_t^\varepsilon(x)$ solving $\dot X_t^\varepsilon(x)=v_t^\varepsilon(X_t^\varepsilon(x))$, $X_0^\varepsilon(x)=x$. For $\mu_0^\varepsilon$-almost every x the path exists on all of $[0,T]$, the map from x to its path is Borel on this full-measure domain, and for every $t\in[0,T]$,
$$\mu_t^\varepsilon=(X_t^\varepsilon)_\#\mu_0^\varepsilon.$$

items.title: Superposition for finite-action Euclidean continuity equations
items.axiom_use: AC is used for standard-Borel disintegration, Prokhorov extraction, Gaussian regularization and the Countable/Dependent Choice branches of Radon approximation; each use is supplied by the cited item hypotheses.

references.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures, Theorem 8.2.1, PDF pp. 179–182
Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §5.3, PDF pp. 176–178

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $T>0$ and let $(\mu_t,v_t)$ be a narrowly continuous finite-action solution of the continuity equation on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d$. There is a Borel probability law $\eta$ on $C([0,T];\mathbb R^d)$ such that $(e_t)_\#\eta=\mu_t$ for every $t$, and for $\eta$-almost every path $\gamma$, $\gamma$ is absolutely continuous, $\gamma(0)$ has law $\mu_0$, and $\dot\gamma(t)=v_t(\gamma(t))$ for almost every $t$. Its expected path action equals the Eulerian action:
$$\int\!\int_0^T|\dot\gamma(t)|^2dt\,d\eta(\gamma)=\int_0^T\!\int|v_t(x)|^2d\mu_t(x)dt.$$

items.title: Finite-action continuity equations generate AC2 Wasserstein curves
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the superposition and scalar metric-derivative suppliers; constructing the path couplings and applying Minkowski adds no choice.

references.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures, Theorem 8.3.1, PDF pp. 183–186
Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §5.3, PDF pp. 176–178

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $T>0$ and let $(\mu_t,v_t)$ be a narrowly continuous finite-action solution of the continuity equation on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^d$. Then $t\mapsto\mu_t$ belongs to $AC^2([0,T];\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d))$ and, for almost every $t$,
$$|\dot\mu_t|\le\left(\int|v_t(x)|^2d\mu_t(x)\right)^{1/2}.$$

items.title: AC2 curves admit a unique minimum-action velocity field
items.axiom_use: AC supplies Countable Choice for Hilbert Riesz and the scalar Lebesgue FTC. The coupling estimates and localization use no further selections.

references.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures, Theorem 8.3.1 and §8.4, PDF pp. 183–190
Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §5.3, PDF pp. 176–178

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $T>0$ and $\mu\in AC^2([0,T];\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d))$. There is a Borel vector field $v$ of finite action that solves the continuity equation and satisfies
$$\int|v_t(x)|^2d\mu_t(x)=|\dot\mu_t|^2$$
for almost every $t$. Every other Borel finite-action solution $w$ of the same continuity equation obeys the pointwise Pythagorean identity
$$\int|w_t(x)|^2d\mu_t(x)=|\dot\mu_t|^2+\int|w_t(x)-v_t(x)|^2d\mu_t(x)$$
for almost every $t$. Consequently $v$ is the unique minimum-action velocity up to $dt\,\mu_t(dx)$-null sets and
$$\int_0^T|\dot\mu_t|^2dt=\min_w\int_0^T\!\int|w_t(x)|^2d\mu_t(x)dt,$$
where the minimum ranges over Borel finite-action fields solving the same continuity equation.

title: Wasserstein metric and continuity-equation foundations — Examples

items.title: Translation of a Dirac mass
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the minimum-velocity theorem; the explicit calculation itself is choice-free.

references.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures, Theorem 8.3.1, PDF pp. 183–186
Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §5.3, PDF pp. 176–178

items.statement: Assume AC. Let $T>0$ and $a,b\in\mathbb R^d$. The curve $\mu_t=\delta_{a+tb}$ belongs to $AC^2([0,T];\mathcal P_2(\mathbb R^d))$, has constant metric speed $|b|$, and the Borel field $v_t(x)=b$ solves the continuity equation. Its action is $T|b|^2$, equal to the minimum action among fields solving that equation for this curve.

items.title: An isotropic Gaussian Wasserstein geodesic
items.axiom_use: AC is inherited from the standard-normal and minimum-velocity suppliers; it also supplies Countable Choice for the finite-product Lebesgue identity; the coupling bounds and interpolation calculation add no choice.

references.title: Luigi Ambrosio, Nicola Gigli, and Giuseppe Savaré, Gradient Flows in Metric Spaces and in the Space of Probability Measures, Theorem 8.3.1, PDF pp. 183–186
Filippo Santambrogio, Optimal Transport for Applied Mathematicians, Chapter 5, §5.3, PDF pp. 176–178

items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $d\ge1$, $m_0,m_1\in\mathbb R^d$, and $\sigma_0,\sigma_1>0$. Let $\xi$ have density $(2\pi)^{-d/2}e^{-|z|^2/2}$ on $\mathbb R^d$, put $m_t=(1-t)m_0+tm_1$ and $\sigma_t=(1-t)\sigma_0+t\sigma_1$, and set $\mu_t=\operatorname{Law}(m_t+\sigma_t\xi)$ for $0\le t\le1$. Then $\mu_t$ is a constant-speed $W_2$ geodesic, meaning $W_2(\mu_s,\mu_t)=|t-s|W_2(\mu_0,\mu_1)$ for all $s,t\in[0,1]$, from the laws of $m_0+\sigma_0\xi$ to the law of $m_1+\sigma_1\xi$, with
$$W_2(\mu_0,\mu_1)^2=|m_1-m_0|^2+d(\sigma_1-\sigma_0)^2.$$
The Borel field
$$v_t(x)=m_1-m_0+\frac{\sigma_1-\sigma_0}{\sigma_t}(x-m_t)$$
solves the continuity equation and has action equal to this squared distance, hence is minimum-action. The strict positivity of $\sigma_0$ and $\sigma_1$ ensures $\sigma_t>0$ throughout; degenerate covariances are excluded.
